source.section: Form 1 lines 2a, 2c (age 65 or over before 2026, 700 each spouse, PDF p10 Line 2c), 4, 9 (Schedule X line 2 worksheet, PDF p20), 10-22; Social Security not taxed (PDF p10 Line 4 note)

worked: Federal AGI = private pension 40,000.00 (person 0) + IRA distribution 20,000.00 (person 1) + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 (30,000.00 gross; provisional income 60,000.00 + 15,000.00 = 75,000.00; 0.85 x (75,000.00 - 44,000.00) + 6,000.00 = 32,350.00, capped at 0.85 x 30,000.00 = 25,500.00) = 85,500.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 85,500.00 - 34,700.00 standard deduction (31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 age 65 or older) = 50,800.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 40,000.00 private pension (taxed: most private pensions are taxable, PDF p10) = 40,000.00. Line 9 (Schedule X line 2 worksheet: 20,000.00 IRA distributions less 0.00 contributions previously taxed by Massachusetts) = 20,000.00. Social Security (30,000.00 gross, 25,500.00 federally taxable) is not reported: Massachusetts does not tax it (PDF p10). Line 10 total 5.0% income = 60,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 60,000.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (married_joint) = 8,800.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 2 x 700.00 = 1,400.00; line 2g = line 18 = 10,200.00. Line 19 = 60,000.00 - 10,200.00 = 49,800.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 49,800.00. Line 22 = 49,800.00 x 0.05 = 2,490.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 2,490.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 60,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 2,490.00.
